text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Three Danish aid organisations, Red Cross, Save the Child and DanChurch Aid are to cooperate with the Danish foreign ministry on creating a special new type of aid programme for Etiopia, combining traditional disaster assistance with developmental aid.

--- Danish transport minister Jan Troejborg is not to increase state support for Danish Rail (DSB), meaning major staff cuts and reduced passenger services. DSB's 1997-98 deficit is expected to be about one billion crowns.
--- Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark is to be taken to court by local telephone sex firm MSB-Denmark for closing down foreign lines.
--- Denmark's Confederation of Industry fears that a decrease in Danish unemployment from 250,000 jobless to 244,000 could lead to a lack of qualified labour in future.

--- Danish dairy group MD Foods is to form a new joint company with Sweden's Arla Dairy in November moving its production of cappuccino essence and chocolate powder to the south of Sweden. The new company will have an estimated annual turnover of 300 million crowns.

--- Copenhagen police has been holding meetings with a number of immigrant organisations with the aim of improving relations and avoiding future conflicts between local police and foreign residents in the capital.
